To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

deep residual networks can be used to improve the accuracy of lung nodule classification, that curriculum learning is effective for improving the training process of deep neural networks, and that transfer learning is effective at leveraging existing knowledge in the form of pretrained networks.

we have developed a novel system that uses deep residual networks, curriculum learning, transfer-learning, and data augmentation to classify pulmonary nodules with the highest accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity.

(1) deep residual networks are effective for lung nodule malignity classification; (2) curriculum learning improves classification performance; (3) transfer learning improves performance when training on a small dataset; and (4) our proposed system achieves state-of-the-art results on the LID-C/IDRI dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving nodule malignancy prediction by leveraging the power of very deep residual learning and transfer learning.
the development of a deep learning based system for pulmonary nodule malignancy detection.
the development of a computer-aided system for the detection of pulmonary nodules.

our system outperforms all existing deep learning systems in terms of all performance measures, and is also more robust to the choice of training data.
our system is the first system to use very deep neural networks to achieve the best performance in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and AUROC on the LIDCI/IDRI dataset.

the proposed method of combining very deep convolutional networks, curriculum learning, transfer-learning and a novel data augmentation strategy results in the highest performance on a standard benchmark dataset.

we are able to achieve a high nodule classification performance by combining the deep residual learning, transfer learning and curriculum learning.
